correctness.rationale: For each n>=2 and oracle A, each finite binary cylinder [sigma] is a positive-measure computable Pi^0_1(A^(n-2)) forcing condition. The dense decision construction of Veltri Lemma 3.18/Cor. 3.19 can start below [sigma], giving a Pi^0_n(A)-generic point there. Inclusion makes the weak class dense too. At each k, the 2^k dyadic cylinders of diameter 2^-k cover; points in two distinct cylinders have distance >2^-k, so any cover by sets of that diameter needs >=2^k sets. Hence exact N_k=2^k and both box dimensions 1, while Veltri Cor. 3.24 and inclusion give Hausdorff dimension 0. All k,n,A from proof, not experiments.

evidence: Veltri proves the forcing dense-decision property and existence for arbitrary positive-measure closed conditions and Hausdorff dimension zero; standard geometry gives full box dimension of any dense subset of Cantor space. Neither source states the exact application N_k(G)=2^k.
